author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Bob Mackie, the fashion and costume designer whose theatrical work helped define Hollywood glamour in the 1970s, died Monday at age 87, The Associated Press reported.
Mackie became known for elaborate costumes built with sequins, rhinestones and bold silhouettes. His work dressed stars including Cher, Carol Burnett, Marilyn Monroe, Madonna and Diana Ross.

His career included television, film, Broadway and fashion. AP reported that Mackie won nine Emmy Awards, received a Tony Award and earned multiple Academy Award nominations. He also designed clothing for Barbie dolls and created costumes that became part of American pop-culture history.

Mackie’s longtime association with Cher produced some of his most recognizable work, while his designs for The Carol Burnett Show demonstrated his ability to combine comedy with high-fashion spectacle.
His publicist said Mackie died in Palm Springs from pneumonia. Tributes are expected to focus on a career that treated costume design as both entertainment and visual storytelling.
dek: The fashion and costume designer whose work shaped 1970s Hollywood glamour died Monday in Palm Springs, according to The Associated Press.
headline: Bob Mackie, designer to the stars, dies at 87
